We pair it with API […] The post Best AI Video Generation Models in 2026: Elo, Price per Second, Open Weights appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> The AI video leaderboard looks very different from 12 months ago. Native audio is now table stakes. Clips run 15–30 seconds. And an open-weights model sits in the top 3. This ranking (as of Nov 13, 2026) uses one quality signal: blind human-preference Elo from the Artificial Analysis Video Arena . We pair it with API price per second and the license status of the weights. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension . Methodology Quality : Artificial Analysis ranks models by Elo from blind pairwise votes by validated evaluators . Each vote compares 2 clips from the same prompt. We rank by the AA-Video-T2V v2.1 (with audio) board. We also report the AA-Video-I2V v2.1 score. Anchor : Kling 3.0 1080p (Pro) is fixed at 1000 Elo on both boards. A score below 1000 means voters preferred Kling 3.0 more often. Price : Artificial Analysis lists cost per minute on each creator’s API. It normalizes to 1080p where offered. We divide by 60 to get price per second. Vendor rates at 720p are often lower, and we flag those gaps. Confidence : Most top-10 scores carry a ±13 to ±15 Elo interval. Models within ~25 points are statistically close. Treat ranks 3–8 as a cluster, not a strict order. The Rankings 1. Alibaba Wan 3.0: Best overall text-to-video T2V Elo: 1175 (#1) · I2V Elo: 1108 (#11) Price: $0.20/sec at 1080p Weights: Closed Wan 3.0 holds the top text-to-video spot with 7,651 votes behind it. Alibaba launched it on August 24, 2026 . It generates 30-second 1080p clips from text, PDFs and slide decks, priced at $0.20 per second. The document-to-video input is the differentiator. You can hand it a deck and get a structured video back. The trade-off is openness. There are no downloadable weights for Wan 3.0 . Wan 2.2 (July 2025) remains Alibaba’s last open video flagship . Note the I2V gap too: Wan 3.0 drops to 11th on image-to-video. Best for: long single takes, explainer videos from existing documents. 2. Utopai Studios Utopai X: Highest-ranked post-train, no API T2V Elo: 1170 (#2) · I2V Elo: 1151 (#2) Price: No public API Weights: Closed Utopai X is the only model in the top 2 on both boards. Utopai Studios, a Mountain View film studio, built it by post-training MiniMax H3 . It beats the base H3 it came from. Access runs only through Utopai’s PAI platform. PAI charges 93 credits per second , with plans starting at $15 for 1,000 credits. Developers cannot call it from a pipeline. Best for: filmmakers working inside a studio tool. Not for programmatic use. 3. MiniMax H3: Best open-weights model T2V Elo: 1161 (#3) · I2V Elo: 1133 (#4) Price: $0.08/sec Weights: Open, under the MiniMax H3 Community License H3 is the first open-weights model in the video top tier. MiniMax launched the API on July 31, 2026 and published weights on August 3 . It is a 33B dense single-stream Transformer, using Qwen3-VL-32B as its encoder . It outputs video with native 32 kHz stereo audio. Read the license before you download. The Hugging Face weights carry real limits: Territory: the license blocks local deployment in the US, EU, UK and South Korea . Resolution: only H3-Base is open, with a 768p ceiling. 2K upscaling stays API-only. Size: the repo holds 2 task-specific checkpoints totaling 288 GB . Even so, H3 has become the base layer of 2026 video. Utopai X, HeyGen Video 1, fal’s H3 Max and Pika H3 Flex are all post-trains of it. AA also lists Pruna’s P-Video-2-Pro as a MiniMax collaboration. Best for: teams outside excluded regions that want to fine-tune a frontier video model. 4. ByteDance Dreamina Seedance 2.5: Best image-to-video T2V Elo: 1155 (#4) · I2V Elo: 1161 (#1) Price: $0.569/sec on AA’s normalized basis Weights: Closed Seedance 2.5 leads image-to-video. ByteDance began rolling it out on July 31, 2026 through Jimeng AI and Doubao Pro. It supports up to 30-second generations with up to 30 image, 10 video and 10 audio references . Pricing needs care. AA lists $34.12 per minute, the highest on the board. BytePlus lists $1.156 for a 5-second 720p clip without video input , or about $0.23/sec. Confirm API access in your region before planning around it. Best for: reference-heavy, image-led ad and character work. 5. Google Gemini Omni Flash 1.2: Best frontier price-to-quality T2V Elo: 1154 (#5) · I2V Elo: 1086 (#14) Price: $0.104/sec on AA’s basis; $0.07/sec at 720p per Google Weights: Closed Gemini Omni Flash 1.2 is the newest entry, generally available since November 5, 2026 . It added 3–15 second clips and a 30% price cut over version 1.1. Video output costs $12 per 1M tokens, about $0.070 per second at 720p . It jumped 27 Elo over Omni Flash 1.1 on text-to-video. Requests to 1.1 route to 1.2 from December 3, 2026 . Best for: teams already on the Gemini API who want a top-5 model under $0.11/sec. 6. fal FLUX 3 Max: Fastest near-frontier generation T2V Elo: 1153 (#6) · I2V Elo: 1068 (#16) Price: $0.145/sec Weights: Closed fal Research post-trained FLUX 3 Max with Black Forest Labs , launching it October 19, 2026. fal says a 10-second 720p clip renders in about 12 seconds . Seedance 2.5 took 277.80 seconds in fal’s own comparison. It shares an API with fal’s H3 Max. Switching between them takes a single model-ID change. Best for: latency-sensitive pipelines and rapid iteration. 7.
